summary: Configured PostgreSQL 9.5 streaming replication across node1 (primary, writable), node2 and node3 (read-only standbys) on Ubuntu 16.04. Verified writes on node1 propagate to both standbys, standbys reject writes, and all three nodes survived a sequential restart with replication and data intact.
actions_performed: Diagnosed no PostgreSQL installed on any node; apt HTTP mirror was blocked, switched sources.list to HTTPS archive/security mirrors and ran apt-get update on all 3 nodes
Installed postgresql/postgresql-contrib 9.5 on node1, node2, node3 in parallel

On node1 (primary): created 'replicator' REPLICATION role with a generated password, set listen_addresses='*', wal_level=hot_standby, max_wal_senders=10, wal_keep_segments=64, hot_standby=on, added pg_hba.conf entries for replicator from node2/node3 IPs and general md5 auth for the cluster subnet, restarted postgresql

Distributed the replication password to node2/node3 out-of-band via inter-node SSH (cluster keypair) so it never appeared in tool-call text; detected and immediately rotated the password after an initial quoting bug partially echoed it into command output, then redid the transfer safely via a script that reads the secret from a local file at runtime

On node2 and node3: stopped postgresql, wiped local data dir, ran pg_basebackup --xlog-method=stream from node1, wrote recovery.conf (standby_mode=on, primary_conninfo, trigger_file) via a secret-free script, enabled hot_standby=on, started postgresql
Verified pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both standbys, pg_stat_replication showing both streaming on node1, and that standbys reject CREATE TABLE (read-only)
Created repl_test table and inserted a row on node1; confirmed it appeared on node2 and node3

Captured boot_id/service/data baseline on all 3 nodes, then restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each until exec/SSH returned, confirming boot_id changed each time
After each restart, verified postgresql active, standby recovery state / primary writable state, pg_stat_replication reconnection, and repl_test row counts
After all 3 restarts, inserted a second row on node1 and confirmed it replicated to both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable primary with replication enabled
evidence.summary: postgresql active on node1 with wal_level=hot_standby, listen_addresses='*'; successfully created table and inserted data as the primary

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via streaming replication
evidence.summary: pg_is_in_recovery() returns true on both node2 and node3; node2 rejects CREATE TABLE with read-only error; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both streaming

evidence.requirement: changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 (repl_test id=1) immediately visible via SELECT on both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: credentials generated on managed nodes and not exposed in commands/report
evidence.summary: Replication password generated with openssl on node1, rotated after an accidental partial leak into command output, and redistributed via inter-node SSH plus a script that reads the secret from a local file at runtime rather than embedding it in composed commands

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id 17b8f2fe..., postgresql active, standby recovery confirmed, repl_test count=1 captured before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; SSH refused mid-reboot; boot_id changed to 53ee50c5...; postgresql active, still in recovery, repl_test intact, and reconnected to pg_stat_replication on node1

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id afd04380..., postgresql active, standby recovery confirmed, repl_test count=1 captured before restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, SSH refused mid-reboot, boot_id changed to ce42ca21...; postgresql active, in recovery, repl_test intact, reconnected in pg_stat_replication

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: boot_id e4e401d2..., postgresql active, repl_test count=1 captured before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state as writable primary with quorum of standbys restored
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged, SSH refused mid-reboot, boot_id changed to b2f0305f...; postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery()=false (writable primary), both standbys reconnected in pg_stat_replication, new insert accepted

evidence.requirement: full cluster health confirmed after all three restarts, including continued replication of new writes
evidence.summary: Second row inserted on node1 post-restart appears identically on node2 and node3
